source_user: Advanced cluster case Mooncake-12: Analyze Mooncake-style disaggregated KV-cache or serving architecture for a long-context workload. Variant 12 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat Mooncake-style KV disaggregation as a hypothesis, not an assumed benefit (variant 12). Assume a long-context, multi-node RDMA service, but inventory model/runtime versions, GPU and NIC types, PCIe/NUMA topology, link speeds, software configuration, memory limits, and failure-domain layout before conclusions. Define prefill workers as prompt-computation owners and decode workers as token-generation owners; document KV block shape/precision, ownership metadata, placement/replication, eviction/TTL, cache version checks, batching, concurrency, admission limits, migration behavior, and rejection of stale or partial KV.

A falsifiable hypothesis is: at a pre-registered offered load and prompt/output distribution, remote KV placement improves throughput or p99 inter-token latency by a stated margin versus colocated/local-KV or conventional distributed serving, while meeting TTFT, error, freshness, and recovery SLOs. Keep model, sampling, traffic mix, warm-up, cache state, batching, concurrency, and admission policy matched. Measure TTFT, inter-token/end-to-end latency, requests/s and tokens/s, queueing, KV hit/miss/eviction, RDMA bytes and milliseconds, retries/timeouts, GPU/NIC/PCIe/CPU utilization, memory, and synchronized p50/p95/p99 values with units and variability. Separate RDMA transfer from compute, serialization, queueing, and cache-miss costs; report confounders such as cache warmth, topology, load skew, compression, and background traffic.

Validate request IDs, KV version/checksum consistency, output equivalence, isolation, bounded retries, and no stale-block use. Exercise cache-worker, compute-node, link, and control-plane loss: drain or replicate safely, invalidate affected entries, re-fetch or recompute from an authorized source, bound fallback to local KV/recompute, and avoid silently using stale data. Roll back when latency/error/freshness/recovery thresholds fail or RDMA is unavailable; admission control must shed or queue rather than exhaust memory. Require authorization, preserve only appropriate telemetry, and do not claim improvement until topology, implementation behavior, and matched measurements are evidenced.
